title: Consolidate compact density tokens and add CI publish validator for Figma library
creator: Maya Chen
description: Audit and reconcile compact/dense token variants used by buttons, tables, and chart controls; standardize canonical token names, provide alias mappings for legacy tokens, fix auto-layout regressions in top-affected instances, and add a lightweight CI validator that blocks Figma library publishes when critical issues are detected.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical compact density token set created and documented in Confluence
Alias mapping CSV produced and applied to automated rename script for legacy tokens
Top 150 instances with layout regressions identified and either automatically fixed or flagged with remediation PRs
Publish validator (Figma plugin + CI hook) implemented to catch: missing token references, broken auto-layout constraints, and renamed component instances before library publish
Design and frontend sign-off on naming conventions and implementation approach
Release notes and migration instructions published alongside the library update
steps: Run project-wide token usage audit via Figma API to list token references by file and component
Create canonical token taxonomy for compact/dense spacing and typography (density-compact, density-compact-2, density-default) and document rationale
Build alias mapping CSV between legacy tokens (e.g., spacing-compact-sm) and new canonical tokens
Write and test a script to apply token renames in batch for files under the design system org
Identify instances with auto-layout warnings and categorize: auto-fixable (simple constraint reset) vs manual review required
Prototype a Figma plugin that validates token references and common auto-layout issues; wire a CI hook to run validations on publish attempts
Create PR template for frontend to accept breaking token renames and surface required code changes (token mapping shim)
Run staged publish to staging library, ask platform design + web eng for verification, then schedule production publish with release notes
decisions: Adopt a 3-tier compact density vocabulary (compact-1, compact-2, default) to balance clarity and developer ergonomics
Prefer alias mappings and migration scripts over manual rework to reduce human error on large file sets
Validator will block publishes for high-severity issues and only warn for medium/low severity to avoid blocking urgent releases
Frontend team will implement a temporary token shim for 2 release cycles to smooth runtime migration
